land.text: the Zaydi highlands of Yemen, lost by the Ottomans' Yemen Eyalet between 1597 and 1636

predecessors.note: Yemen Eyalet infobox: established 1517, 'Succeeded by: Qasimid State; Yemen vilayet'. The Qasimids took the highlands by 1608, Sana'a in 1628, Zabid and Mocha in 1634 and the rest by 1636.

land.text: the Zaydi highlands of Sana'a without the coast

successors.note: The same Zaydi imamate: Cliopatria ends its Qasimids row in 1802 and starts 'Imamate of Yemen' in 1814. This dossier is extended to 1813 so that the two rows meet; the Qasimid State page does not end the state before 1849.

successors.note: Qasimid State page: 'The rising power of the fervent Wahhabi movement cost the Zaidi state its coastal possessions after 1803.'

capitals.name: Sana'a
capitals.note: Infobox capital 'Sanaa'; the Ottomans were expelled from Sana'a in 1628. The pages opened name no seat for 1597-1627; al-Mutawakkil Isma'il is said to have resided at 'al-Suda' (Al-Mutawakkil Isma'il page).

correction.text: Hajjah, whose emir supported al-Qasim, and the Ahnumi tribesmen

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (1597-1607): Cliopatria's first Qasimid shape is 1636, but 'al-Mansur al-Qasim proclaimed the Imamate in September 1597'. The page does not say where; it names the Ahnumi tribesmen, who backed him early, and 'the emir of the important stronghold Hajjah in the western mountains', who 'chose to support al-Qasim'.

correction.text: the Zaydi highlands: 'By 1608, Imam al-Mansur had regained control over the highlands', with Sana'a (Ottoman until 1628) and the Tihama (Ottoman until 1634-1636) left out

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (1608-1627): 'By 1608, Imam al-Mansur had regained control over the highlands and signed a ten-year truce with the Ottomans'; the page does not say which territory each side kept. Sana'a stays Ottoman until 1628 and the Ottomans lose Aden and Lahej in 1627 (Yemen Eyalet page).

minus.text: the Tihama with Zabid and Mocha

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1636 shape without the Ottoman Tihama (Zabid and Mocha) until 1634

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (1628-1633): 'Al-Mu'ayyad Muhammad expelled the Ottomans from Sana'a in 1628, only Zabid and Mocha remained under Ottoman possession', both falling in 1634.

correction.text: the Cliopatria shape of 1636 applied to 1634-1635, when the Ottomans leave Zabid and Mocha

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (1634-1635): 'Al-Mu'ayyad Muhammad captured Zabid in 1634 and allowed the Ottomans to leave Mocha peacefully'; 'by 1636, the Zaydi tribesmen had driven the Ottomans out of the country completely'. The shape is Cliopatria's first Qasimid shape, which starts two years late.

208,000 km2: 'By 1636, the Zaydi tribesmen had driven the Ottomans out of the country completely.' The northern edge (19.2 N) already reaches Asir, which the pages give to al-Mutawakkil Isma'il's conquest ('from Asir in the north to Dhofar in the east'); Najran was an Ottoman gain of 1583 (Yemen Eyalet page). No infobox area exists on the pages opened, so the area check is not made.
Same 208,000 km2. Reign of al-Mu'ayyad Muhammad: the Qasimid State infobox says 1620-1640, the Yemen Eyalet page has him die in 1644.
213,000 km2, south edge 12.63 N: Aden is in. 'Aden had been conquered by Yemeni forces in 1644' (Al-Mutawakkil Isma'il page); the Ottomans had lost Aden and Lahej in 1627.

correction.text: the shape as direct territory, with Hadramaut and Dhofar drawn as vassal tint (vassal_start 1654 and 1658) rather than as part of the state

keyframe_review.note: 361,000 km2, east edge 52.4 E: Hadhramaut and Dhofar are drawn as Qasimid land. The Al-Mutawakkil Isma'il page dates the Hadramaut campaign to 1654 (the Yafa tribesmen and the Kathiri sultan submitted) and 'a further expedition in 1658 renewed the suzerainty of the imam in an area as far east as Dhofar'; the Al-Mahdi Ahmad page says Ahmad 'loosely incorporated Hadramaut' in 1658. That is suzerainty, a vassal tint, not direct rule; Cliopatria draws it 1659 (the Hadramaut part five years late).

166,000 km2 for 1683-1733: Hadhramaut and Dhofar are gone and Aden and Lahej remain. No page opened dates the loss. The Qasimid State page records the succession crisis after al-Mahdi Ahmad's death in 1681 (al-Mu'ayyad Muhammad II chosen, died 1686, seven contenders in three years, al-Mahdi Muhammad in power in 1689); the ledger bridges the vassal_end events to 1683 at confidence 1.

154,000 km2, south edge 13.08 N: Aden and Lahej are gone. 'In 1728 or 1731, the chief representative of Lahij declared himself an independent sultan' and the infobox has 'Secession of Lahej: 1740'; the shape change of 1734 lies inside that span.
Unverified: page budget. 154,000 km2; west edge 42.69 E, a change of a few km2 only. Cliopatria's Emirate of Diriyah is a neighbour from 1794 to 1802 (seed); no page opened dates a clash.
Unverified: page budget. Same area as 1794.
Unverified: page budget. 154,000 km2; Cliopatria's last Qasimid shape, to 1802. The page dates the loss of the coast to 'after 1803', which the 1803 keyframe handles.

correction.text: the 1800 shape without the Tihama, the coast lost to the Wahhabi movement after 1803

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (1803-1813): Cliopatria's row ends in 1802 and the Imamate of Yemen row starts in 1814. 'The rising power of the fervent Wahhabi movement cost the Zaidi state its coastal possessions after 1803.' The page does not name the coast; the Tihama is my reading.

region.text: the Zaydi highlands: 'By 1608, Imam al-Mansur had regained control over the highlands', with Sana'a (Ottoman until 1628) and the Tihama (Ottoman until 1634-1636) left out

ledger.note: 1597: the revolt against the Ottomans. The page dates no first campaign; the contest is dated to the proclamation year (confidence 1). The northern Zaydi tribes, especially the Hashid and Bakil, 'constantly resisted Ottoman imperial rule'.

region.text: Hajjah, whose emir supported al-Qasim, and the Ahnumi tribesmen

ledger.note: September 1597: al-Mansur al-Qasim proclaims the Zaydi imamate. 'Al-Mansur al-Qasim proclaimed the Imamate in September 1597' (infobox 'Proclamation: 1597'). The page names Hajjah's emir and the Ahnumi tribesmen as early supporters, not a place of proclamation.

region.text: the Zaydi highlands: 'By 1608, Imam al-Mansur had regained control over the highlands', with Sana'a (Ottoman until 1628) and the Tihama (Ottoman until 1634-1636) left out

ledger.note: 1608: the ten-year truce. 'By 1608, Imam al-Mansur had regained control over the highlands and signed a ten-year truce with the Ottomans.'

region.text: the Zaydi highlands: 'By 1608, Imam al-Mansur had regained control over the highlands', with Sana'a (Ottoman until 1628) and the Tihama (Ottoman until 1634-1636) left out

ledger.note: 1608: the highlands are Qasimid. 'By 1608, Imam al-Mansur had regained control over the highlands' (the year is the page's 'by 1608'; the extent is my reading).
1628: al-Mu'ayyad Muhammad takes Sana'a. 'After al-Mu'ayyad Muhammad expelled the Ottomans from Sana'a in 1628, only Zabid and Mokha remained under Ottoman control.'

region.text: Zabid, Mocha and the Tihama, the Ottoman remnant

ledger.note: 1628: only the Tihama remains Ottoman. 'Al-Mu'ayyad Muhammad expelled the Ottomans from Sana'a in 1628, only Zabid and Mocha remained under Ottoman possession.'
1634: Zabid falls and the Ottomans leave Mocha. 'Al-Mu'ayyad Muhammad captured Zabid in 1634 and allowed the Ottomans to leave Mocha peacefully.'
1636: the Ottomans are out of Yemen. 'By 1636, the Zaydi tribesmen had driven the Ottomans out of the country completely.'

1644: Aden is conquered. 'Aden had been conquered by Yemeni forces in 1644.' The Ottomans lost Aden and Lahej in 1627 (Yemen Eyalet page) and the pages do not say who held Aden in between, so the counterpart is 'nobody'. Al-Mutawakkil Isma'il, imam from 1644, then took 'Yemen in its entirety, from Asir in the north to Dhofar in the east' (Yemen Eyalet page).

region.text: the Hadramaut: the Yafa tribesmen and the Kathiri sultan submitted

ledger.note: 1654: the imam sends an army into the Hadramaut. A succession struggle among the Kathiri gave him a pretext to 'send a sizable army into the Hadramaut'; the Yafa tribesmen and the Kathiri sultan submitted. The Al-Mahdi Ahmad page speaks of Hadramaut 'loosely incorporated' in 1658.

region.text: Dhofar, the far east of the imam's suzerainty

ledger.counterpart: Dhofar (local rulers; the page names none)
ledger.note: 1658: Dhofar. 'A further expedition in 1658 renewed the suzerainty of the imam in an area as far east as Dhofar.'

The Hadramaut leaves the imam's suzerainty. No page opened dates it; the year is Cliopatria's (the shape shrinks from 361,000 to 166,000 km2 in 1683, two years after the imam al-Mahdi Ahmad died in 1681 and a succession crisis began) (confidence 1).

ledger.counterpart: Dhofar (local rulers; the page names none)
ledger.note: Dhofar leaves the imam's suzerainty; same bridge as the Hadramaut (confidence 1).

region.text: Lahej, whose chief representative declared himself sultan

ledger.note: 1731 (or 1728): Lahej breaks away. 'In 1728 or 1731, the chief representative of Lahij declared himself an independent sultan'; in 1740 'the 'Abdali sultan of Lahij became completely independent' (infobox 'Secession of Lahej: 1740'). Cliopatria draws the loss in 1734.

region.text: the coastal possessions, the Tihama (my reading)

ledger.note: 1803: the Wahhabis take the coast. 'The rising power of the fervent Wahhabi movement cost the Zaidi state its coastal possessions after 1803.' The page names neither the coast nor the taker's state; the Emirate of Diriyah is the Wahhabi state in Cliopatria.

region.text: the Zaydi highlands, passing to Cliopatria's Imamate of Yemen row from 1814

ledger.note: 1813: the Cliopatria row changes. The Qasimid State page does not end the state in 1813 (its infobox has 'Reincorporation into Ottoman Empire: 1849'); the same Zaydi imamate continues as Cliopatria's Imamate of Yemen from 1814, so the dissolve is a bridge between two rows (confidence 1).

wars.name: Qasimid revolt against the Ottomans (1597-1636)

zones.text: the Zaydi highlands: 'By 1608, Imam al-Mansur had regained control over the highlands', with Sana'a (Ottoman until 1628) and the Tihama (Ottoman until 1634-1636) left out

wars.outcome: The Qasimids win the highlands (1608, ten-year truce), Sana'a (1628) and Zabid and Mocha (1634); the Ottomans are out of the country by 1636.
wars.note: The Qasimid State page has the proclamation (September 1597), the truce of 1608 and the loss of Aden and Lahej in 1627.

wars.name: Qasimid conquest of the Hadramaut and Dhofar (1654-1658)
wars.outcome: The Yafa tribesmen and the Kathiri sultan submit (1654); an expedition of 1658 renews the imam's suzerainty as far east as Dhofar.

wars.name: Qasimid succession crisis (1681-1689)
wars.outcome: After al-Mahdi Ahmad's death in 1681 relatives at Rada, Shaharah, Sa'dah and Mansura contest the succession; al-Mu'ayyad Muhammad II is chosen through the ulama and dies in 1686, and al-Mahdi Muhammad takes power in 1689 after a violent struggle. No frontier change is dated.

wars.name: Secession of Lahej (1728-1740)
wars.outcome: The Abdali chief of Lahej declares himself sultan in 1728 or 1731 and becomes completely independent in 1740.

wars.name: Wahhabi conquest of the Qasimid coast (after 1803)
wars.outcome: The Wahhabi movement costs the Zaidi state its coastal possessions after 1803; the page gives no battle or date.

certainty.note: Highland tribal imamate: no treaty lines; the Aden and Lahej edge, the Hadramaut and Dhofar suzerainties and the Tihama coast are approximate, and the Hadramaut and Dhofar are drawn as vassal tint.

notes:
Cliopatria rows: the Qasimids row (1636-1802) begins 39 years after the proclamation of 1597 and ends in 1802, 12 years before the 'Imamate of Yemen' row (1814-1872, imamate-of-yemen) of the same Zaydi imamate; this dossier starts in 1597 with four new keyframes (1597, 1608, 1628, 1634) and runs to 1813 with one (1803), so that the two rows meet. The 1813 dissolve is a bridge at confidence 1; the Qasimid State page keeps the state alive to 1849 ('Reincorporation into Ottoman Empire: 1849') and the Yemen Eyalet page has the Ottomans take Sana'a in 1872. A gap-filler may prefer to end this dossier with the imamate-of-yemen dossier merged in.

The 1659-1682 shape (Hadhramaut and Dhofar as direct land) is marked adjust: the pages call it suzerainty (vassal tint). The loss of both in the 1680s is undated on the pages opened (Cliopatria, 1683, confidence 1).

Page budget: 5 pages plus a disambiguation page (Ottoman Yemen). The Rassid dynasty page is thin (no territory); the 1597-1608 extent, the reason for the 1683 shrink, the 1794-1802 changes and the Wahhabi coast of 1803 are not dated or located by any page opened. No page gives an infobox area, so the area check is not made.

Region names: 'Mocha' (Al Mukha) is missing from the gazetteer places, so the Tihama region stands in for it; 'Tihama', 'Hadramawt', 'Dhofar' and 'Aden (region)' resolve. The 'Kathiri sultanate (Hadhramaut)', 'Sultanate of Lahej' and 'Dhofar (local rulers)' counterparts have no dossier; the Sultanate of Lahej (Abdali) may deserve one (1728-1839, Qasimid State page). 'Rulers' is omitted: the pages give only fragments of the imam list (al-Mansur al-Qasim 1597-1620, al-Mu'ayyad Muhammad 1620-1640 or 1644, al-Mutawakkil Isma'il 1644-1676, al-Mahdi Ahmad 1676-1681, al-Mu'ayyad Muhammad II to 1686, al-Mahdi Abbas 1748-1775).
